Terms of Reference

1. Background and Context
MdM Spain together with its European partners (MdM Belgium and MdM UK) has responded
as a Consortium to the EU Aid Volunteers Initiative Call of the European Union.
1.1 Presentation and Objectives of EU Aid Volunteers Initiative
- Complement current humanitarian interventions with the deployment of volunteers
with a view to supporting local organizations to deliver needs-based humanitarian aid,
while also building the capacity and resilience of local communities affected by
disasters globally.
- Strengthen capacities of sending and hosting organizations participating or planning to
participate in the EU Aid Volunteers Initiative.
Moreover, as MdM participates as a Consortium in the Deployment in the framework of the
EU Aid Volunteers Initiative, it is necessary to implement the mentioned project, following the
3 main EU Regulations:
4. Regulation Nº 375/2014: establishes the European Voluntary Humanitarian Aid Corps
(= “EU Aid Volunteers Initiative”)
5. Implementing Regulation Nº 1244/2014: establishes volunteer management
procedures, training programme, certification mechanism
6. Delegated Regulation Nº 1398/2014: establishes standards on recognition, equal
opportunities, partnerships and the competence framework
